title: A small local services bid with 19 requirements and no room for error
description: This fictional local professional-services scenario has a narrow scope and a short response window. The effort is concentrated in showing relevant experience and following a strict submission format.
The example assumes 14 days and a value under $500K. The authored counts are illustrative; no specific live bid, agency, company, or actual extraction result is represented.

gapPreview.requirement: Keep technical and price material in the required separate envelopes.
gapPreview.flag: Provide source-backed company evidence and have a reviewer assess this requirement.

gapPreview.requirement: Verify the labeling and placement of each submission component.
gapPreview.flag: Verify the required attachment is present and current.

gapPreview.requirement: Check that the experience evidence supports the proposed professional services.
gapPreview.flag: Provide source-backed company evidence and have a reviewer assess this requirement.

dealBreakers: The fictional instructions use a two-envelope rule: technical and price material must stay separate. Placing price information in the wrong envelope leads to rejection under the example’s stated rule.
lesson: Short deadlines plus strict submission rules punish copy-paste bids. Build the submission checklist first, then have a second reviewer check packaging and separation before delivery.

faq.question: Where do teardowns come from?
faq.answer: These launch teardowns are authored fictional examples based on common solicitation shapes. Their counts are illustrative, not measured results from real bids or visitor submissions.

faq.question: Can I get my solicitation torn down?
faq.answer: Use the free shredder or bid checker privately. A public teardown requires separate human review, anonymization, and your explicit confirmation. Publication is never automatic.

faq.question: Does a teardown guarantee anything?
faq.answer: No. A teardown does not certify compliance or predict an award. Verify the original solicitation, attachments, and amendments before making a bid decision.
